# HButtonBar

> Group actions without changing native button focus or submission behavior.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HButtonBar` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-button-bar>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthButtonBarElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HButtonBar.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- This is a labeled role=group, not a toolbar with custom arrow-key navigation.
- Children keep their native focus, click, and form behavior. Explicitly choose submit/reset types as needed.
- align supports start, center, end, and between. orientation controls horizontal or vertical layout.

## Public API

label: string · align: start | center | end | between · orientation: horizontal | vertical

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label?: string;
    align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "between";
    orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical";
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ label: "Actions", align: "start", orientation: "horizontal" }
```

### Events

None (children retain their own events)

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base

Use `hearth-button-bar::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HButtonBar, HButton } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
function cancel() { /* Close or reset your editor. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HButtonBar label="Form actions" align="end">
    <HButton @click="cancel">Cancel</HButton>
    <HButton type="submit" variant="primary">Save</HButton>
  </HButtonBar>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-button-bar');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Form actions",
  "align": "end"
});
element.innerHTML = "<hearth-button type=\"button\">Cancel</hearth-button>\n<hearth-button type=\"submit\" variant=\"primary\">Save</hearth-button>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.
mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HButton](../button/llms.txt): Native button or link behavior, clear focus, icon-only labels, and restrained press feedback.
- [HDialog](../dialog/llms.txt): A native modal dialog with focus containment, Escape dismissal, and focus return. Keep it inside your theme island.
- [HCard](../card/llms.txt): The common surface: restrained depth, a readable heading, and generous space for your content.
